passages.text: Sadleria cyatheoides, commonly known as amaumau fern or amau, is a fern species in the family Blechnaceae.

Description 
Reaching a height of {{convert|0.9|-|1.5|m|ft|abbr=on|frac=2}} and a trunk diameter of {{convert|7.5|-|10|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}}, {{okina}}ama{{okina}}u resembles a small tree fern.
The young fronds are often tinged red to block harmful sunlight.

Distribution and habitat 
It is endemic to Hawaii and inhabits lava flows, open areas, and wet forests on all major islands up to an altitude of {{convert|1676|m|ft|abbr=on}}.

Uses 
Its pith and young fronds are edible either roasted or steamed.

In culture 
Kīlauea's Halemaʻumaʻu is named for this species.
